correctness.rationale: The proof reduces the full Banach-Mazur problem to diagonal quadratic forms by sign averaging, derives necessary and sufficient inner constraints by weighted Cauchy-Schwarz, reduces the outer factor exactly to two polygon vertices, and solves the resulting global one-dimensional minimax problem in all feasible regimes. The balance and endpoint formulas, feasibility thresholds, regime exhaustiveness, and equality-boundary agreement were algebra-checked; numerical tests were only stress tests and are not used as proof.

value.rationale: The extreme points of the convex set of absolute normalized norms are a canonical structural family. Their interior asymmetric portion is genuinely two-parameter, and the theorem gives its complete exact Euclidean distortion phase diagram together with an optimal ellipse in every regime. This is a natural classification, not a renamed special case or arbitrary parameter slice.
